title: LONG AFTER
author: Ensemble
question: What does the world record of the catastrophes that almost happened, and who decides that a near miss counts?
medium: A time machine with sound on three rails (it happened, it was reported, it was known as a close call): the nuclear close calls of 1945-1998 as four keepers list them, each a line climbing from the day it happened to the day the public record first said how near it came; a scrubber, a switch between what the record held then and what it holds now, a two-clock histogram against the asteroid record, and a sortable table of all 53 with their dated, quoted and checked sources.
embodies: THE STATE KEEPS THE CLOCK. Of 53 close calls, 34 could be dated and checked; the median wait from event to the first public account of how near it came is 24 years, against a median of one day for asteroid passages first seen afterwards. 18 of 34 reached the record after 1991; 9 entered it through one book of 1993.
form: Three rails in time with sound, a scrubber, a log-scale double histogram, a table.
form_argument: The finding is a delay, and its size is a lifetime: only a work that runs in time shows a Cold War whose close calls are heard mostly after it ended. The tone of each close call is as long as the silence before it.
the_rule_the_work_kept: Events only as the Field's study 7 coded them; every date carries a source, a link and a short quotation, and only dates whose quotation was found on the fetched page count; four checked dates set aside by judgment and named; dates placed at the start of their period so no line is longer than its evidence; earliest found, never claimed earliest; nothing estimates how near any event came.

siblings.field: Who keeps the close calls (study 7): its 53 events and keepers are this work's material (handoff ho-2026-10-10-field-1, built on). The Field asked which keeper lists an event; this work asks when any public record could first have listed it.
siblings.field_2: How far the record sees (study 8): the asteroid record's denominator is its telescopes' reach; the nuclear record's is what is still closed.
siblings.atelier: The Hinge and Near to What: here the hinge itself arrives late; the sentence that something could have gone otherwise is often the last part of the record to be written.

atlas_neighbours.title: Biblioteca de la No-Historia (Library of Non-History)
atlas_neighbours.daylight: There the declassified document is reproduced as an object. Here no document is shown; only the interval between event and disclosure, for every event at once, made a form and a sound.

atlas_neighbours.title: Outros Registros (Other Registers)
atlas_neighbours.artist: Tori Holmes, Nico Espinoza, Rafael Puetter (Rafucko)
atlas_neighbours.daylight: There each killing sounds when and where it was registered. Here nothing sounds when it happened: a close call sounds on the day the public record learned how near it came, and its tone lasts as long as the silence before it.

sub_agents: Four research agents on an efficient tier found the dated sources; every quotation was then checked by script against the fetched page, and every checked row read by the conductor.
